name: DeepRetinotopy
summary: DeepRetinotopy brainlife.io app: predict retinotopic maps from cortical anatomy using geometric deep learning. Based on the original deepRetinotopy model by Fernanda L. Ribeiro et al. (2021, 2024, 2025).
description: Wraps deepRetinotopy_TheToolbox (Neurodesk vnmd/deepretinotopy container): builds midthickness surfaces and curvature from the native FreeSurfer white/pial surfaces, resamples them to the HCP 32k fs_LR mesh, predicts polar angle, eccentricity and pRF size with a pretrained geometric deep learning model, and maps the predictions back to native surfaces and the T1 volume, with a visual-area parcellation. Use it to estimate retinotopic maps when no retinotopic mapping scan is available. Needs only lh/rh white, pial and sphere.reg surfaces; no FreeSurfer license is required.

inputs.description: A single subject's FreeSurfer output directory.
inputs.requirements: surf/ must contain lh/rh white, pial and sphere.reg.

outputs.description: Predicted polar angle, eccentricity and pRF size (rfWidth) maps with a visual-area parcellation and cortical mask, as T1-space volumes and native-surface GIFTIs (prf_surfaces/), plus surface meshes.

parameters.description: Comma-separated maps to predict: polarAngle, eccentricity, pRFsize
Dataset label passed to the deepRetinotopy toolbox
Internal subject id used when staging the FreeSurfer input
Fast midthickness generation: yes or no
Pass --nv to Singularity for GPU-accelerated inference
vnmd/deepretinotopy container tag to pull (default: 1.0.18; use 1.0.19 if your resource has Apptainer >= 1.5.3)
Fold polar angle from 0-360° to 0-180° (Benson/neuropythy convention; hemisphere encodes left vs right visual field)
Use NaN-aware barycentric interpolation for surface-to-volume projection (non-finite vertices get zero weight; disable if results look worse than standard prism projection)

citations.text: Ribeiro FL, Bollmann S, Puckett AM. Predicting the retinotopic organization of human visual cortex from anatomy using geometric deep learning. NeuroImage 118624 (2021).
Ribeiro FL, et al. Predicting functional topography of the human visual cortex from cortical anatomy at scale. bioRxiv (2025).
Renton AI, et al. Neurodesk: an accessible, flexible and portable data analysis environment for reproducible neuroimaging. Nat Methods 21(5):804-808 (2024).
Hayashi S, et al. brainlife.io: a decentralized platform for reproducible neuroscience. Nat Methods (2024).

failure_modes.message: 'freesurfer' must point at a single subject's FreeSurfer output directory
failure_modes.fix: Provide a FreeSurfer subject directory containing surf/.
